item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AHEAD of next year’s elections, the National leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has already predicted an overwhelming victory for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. They said the platform presents a formidable pathway to victory for the party. Read Also: * * 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election The party said both the South-East and South-South are firmly blocked, and the North-West and North-East are equally blocked for Obi/ Kwankwaso for January 16, 2027 presidential election. According to the NDC, the 2023 election already demonstrated Obi’s clear electoral strength across the North-Central, where he carried Plateau, Nasarawa, and the FCT, stressing that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. Speaking with Vanguard exclusively, the spokesperson, NDC National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu said those who mistake Peter Obi’s gentlemanly demeanor for weakness overlook what she described as the grit and resilience of a leader who grew up navigating the tough, street-smart realities of Onitsha. The NDC National Campaign Council Spokesperson said another major advantage for the party that would contribute to its victory next year is that Kwankwasiyya movement is no pushover when it comes to electoral sturdiness against the backdrop that the group had been tested, it is a disciplined one and ready to defend its mandate at the polls. Ikokwu, who noted that no sensible election rigger would wish to confront the potent combination of the Obidient and Kwankwasiyya (OK) movements, stressed that as many voters demonstrated in the previous cycle, financial inducements on election day will not stop struggling citizens from voting their conscience, adding that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. The NDC said Obi will win the presidential election despite the fact that critics often point to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, boasting over 30 aligned state governors as an insurmountable advantage, stressing that Nigerian political history had proven it that governors do not cast votes, but citizens do. Bala, who spoke in an interview with BBC Hausa on Saturday, said he regarded Atiku as a father figure but was disappointed that the former vice-president had not contacted him amid the leadership crisis rocking the party. He said this while reacting to a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the ADC leadership dispute, adding that he remained willing to work with Atiku, former Senate President David Mark and other party chieftains to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections. Bala said the judgment had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the party, insisting that its position was based on the provisions of the ADC constitution. “Alhamdulillah. item.title: Who Gets To Compete?
item.description: Opposition talks are continuing. Campaigns are gathering pace. But access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming defining questions of the election. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. Together, they reveal a contest in which persuading voters is only part of the task. Candidates must sustain their organisations, establish their right to participate and reach citizens safely. The electoral commission must demonstrate that those citizens’ choices will be recorded faithfully. The week’s developments sharpen a fundamental question: how open, credible and competitive will the road to 2027 remain? Lagos Raises the Stakes Thursday’s reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, deserves particular attention. According to reporting from the scene, armed men disrupted the gathering, participants were injured and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility; the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The report established no independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. Investigation must establish who acted, who organised them and whether anyone provided support. The democratic principle requires no such delay: citizens must be able to attend lawful political meetings without fearing assault. Violence can influence an election before a ballot is cast. It can discourage attendance, make venues reluctant to host meetings, increase campaign costs and persuade volunteers to stay home. Its effects therefore extend beyond the immediate victims. When intimidation restricts participation, it changes the conditions under which candidates compete. Political leaders should condemn attacks consistently, including when the victims support their opponents. Security agencies must provide protection on the same basis. Makinde Keeps the Alliance Door Open Seyi Makinde’s latest comments give fresh substance to the opposition’s continuing conversation about cooperation. In an interview reported today, the Oyo governor confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. He said decisions should draw on evidence, manifestos, previous performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a preferred candidate. That distinction separates a development worth watching from a coalition already formed. The negotiations face a familiar practical difficulty: cooperation requires choices that impose costs on participants. Someone may need to surrender an ambition, accept another candidate’s leadership or persuade supporters to work with former rivals. An agreement also needs to travel beyond the negotiating room. item.title: 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s 2027 presidential ambition is drawing attention amid growing discontent with the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Northern Nigeria, claims of a shift in the late President Muhammadu Buhari’s political support base and mounting public frustration over economic hardship. Read Also: * * Although President Bola Tinubu retains the advantages of incumbency and an extensive political structure, developments in the North, where Atiku has considerable political networks, could provide the former vice-president with an opportunity to mount a formidable challenge in the next presidential election. The emerging political calculations are being driven by Atiku’s renewed mobilisation efforts, claims of a possible realignment of Buhari’s political followers and the growing expectation that economic dissatisfaction could become a major factor in the 2027 contest. Atiku has placed considerable emphasis on Northern voter mobilisation, urging supporters in Sokoto to mobilise their families, friends and communities, turn out massively and protect their ballots. “I appeal to every one of you to come out, mobilise your families, your friends and all well-wishers. Vote massively, protect your vote, and make sure your vote is counted and announced,” he said. He warned that poor turnout could undermine the opposition’s numerical strength. “If you fail to turn out in large numbers, people will go from village to village buying voters’ cards to create the impression that we do not have as many supporters as those in the South,” he warned. The former vice-president’s emphasis on turnout reflects the importance of translating political support into actual votes, particularly in a region whose electoral strength could prove decisive in the next presidential contest. Northern calculations Adding another dimension to Atiku’s Northern calculations, former Minister of Sports and Youth Development, Solomon Dalung, an African Democratic Congress, ADC, chieftain who served under Buhari, claimed that the late president’s political following was shifting towards Atiku. Dalung linked the development to a reported visit by Buhari’s widow, Aisha, to the former vice-president. He described it as evidence of a political realignment. “The message she took for any politician to know is that the 12 million votes have been successfully transferred. We have had a phone call from the grave of Buhari that we should vote Atiku,” he said. He also expressed confidence that Atiku could defeat Tinubu, arguing that the former vice-president remained a formidable political contender despite the challenges facing his platform. “I am confident that as events are unfolding, Tinubu, even if he would take over the ADC secretariat and stop ADC from campaigning, cannot defeat Atiku Abubakar in 2027,” Dalung said. item.title: ‘Truly beautiful’ to make football return, says Ronaldinho
item.description: Brazilian great Ronaldinho says it will be “truly beautiful” to make his return to the pitch on Sunday, 11 years after retirement, when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna. The 46-year-old, who last played for Fluminense in 2015, will start for Ravenna in their local derby against Forli. “I want to have a great day. I’m happy to be here for the start of this wonderful story,” Ronaldinho told Sky Sports on Friday. “The president dreams of something big for Ravenna, and being a part of it makes me happy.” Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani has said his goal is to take the club to Serie A for the first time in their history. The team’s Stadio Bruno Benelli, which usually holds 5,000 fans, is sold out, with a 1,800-capacity temporary stand — dubbed “R10” — also erected for the occasion. Ravenna, who have not even played in Serie B since 2008, are second in their group in Serie C, six points behind leaders Spezia. “Returning to the pitch after so much time is truly beautiful — I’m here to experience a special moment in my life,” added Ronaldinho. “It’s been a few years since I stopped playing — I’ve won everything I ever dreamed of. “Now I’m 46, and I’ve experienced everything there is to experience in football. This is a completely different kind of opportunity. I want to be part of the dream held by my friends who work for Ravenna.” The 2005 Ballon d’Or winner will be hoping to score his 300th career goal, over a decade after he netted his 299th. The former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star has even spent time in a Paraguayan prison since, after attempting to enter the country on a false passport, but did star in a prison futsal match. The move to Ravenna is widely regarded as a marketing stunt, but one Cipriani hopes can help kickstart his Serie A dream. “The long-term goal is to get Ravenna promoted to Serie A,” insisted the club president. item.title: I received N100m alert after APC campaign – Portable
item.description: Nigerian singer, Habeeb Okikiola, popularly known as Portable, has claimed that Ogun State All Progressive Congress governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, also known as Yayi, sent him N100m after he participated in campaign activities for the party. Portable made the claim in a video circulating on social media on Friday, where he expressed excitement over the alleged payment and thanked Adeola and another politician, IBD Dende. In the footage, the singer wore an APC-branded shirt and a cap bearing Yayi’s name, while displaying campaign materials featuring the senator. He explained that IBD Dende had earlier asked him to return home and promised to contact him, but some of his associates later informed him that the senator was looking for him. The singer said he initially doubted the information because of an earlier experience in which he was reportedly told that money had been sent to him, but he received nothing. “My dearest fans! I just woke up to an alert of N100m from Yayi! IBD Dende, oga mi! God bless you. Thank you! Yayi instructed them to send me the money. I took a nap, and God saved me from death,” he said. Portable added that he was initially suspicious when he heard that Adeola wanted to reach him. “Are you the one to tell me that Yayi is looking for me?’ I asked. They wanted to scam me, just as they did when Yayi sent money previously. I did not get a dime then,” he said. “Thank you, Lord! Yayi has sent N100m. Thank you, IBD Dende. May your children be glorious! May you live long, my daddy. It shall be well with you. N100m is not a small amount at all!” he added. The claim comes weeks after Portable publicly acknowledged receiving payments for taking part in APC campaign activities in support of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Amupitan’s resignation report false, misleading — INEC
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has refuted a social media report suggesting that its Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, is set to resign. The commission described the claim, which was shared alongside an image online, as fabricated and misleading. INEC made its position known on Saturday through a statement on its official X account, urging Nigerians to disregard the report and refrain from circulating unverified information. “The claim is FALSE, FABRICATED AND MISLEADING,” the commission stated. “Members of the public are urged to disregard the fabricated report, refrain from sharing unverified information and rely solely on INEC’s official communication channels for authentic information. “Stop the spread of fake news.” Recall Vanguard reported that Amupitan was confronted by protesters outside Chatham House on Thursday, calling for his resignation over alleged shortcomings in the voters’ register. The protesters surrounded his vehicle as he departed a discussion on Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 elections, with some demanding that he step out to address their concerns. item.title: NAFDAC uncovers unregistered cosmetics, falsified medicines, banned soaps at Trade Fair Complex
item.description: By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected illegal cosmetics production and packaging operation at the Tools and Hardware section of Trade Fair Complex, Lagos. The raid exposes a network of unregistered products and materials allegedly intended for illicit manufacturing. Read Also: NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager The discovery followed an enforcement operation at the sprawling market along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. Officials found unlabelled cosmetics, empty product containers, packaging materials and already-produced creams across different floors of a two-storey building. In a video of the operation shared on the Agency’s official X account on Saturday, Mr. Olakunle Ojo, NAFDAC enforcement team lead, and other officials were seen inspecting the building and displaying the recovered materials, raising concerns over the production and circulation of cosmetics of unknown origin and regulatory status. “This is exactly what we are able to find at this particular location,” Mr. Ojo said while displaying various packaging materials and empty containers. The inspection revealed packaging materials bearing names such as turmeric vitamin C and other cosmetic product descriptions, alongside empty shampoo tubes, lotion containers and materials suspected to be intended for the packaging of unregistered products. On the upper floors, officials discovered additional packaging materials, including containers for different cosmetic products, as well as already-produced glutawide cream. The agency also displayed materials bearing different product names, but could not immediately establish the identity and regulatory status of some of the substances and products found at the premises. NAFDAC described the operation as part of its ongoing enforcement activities at the Trade Fair Complex, where it has uncovered several suspected illegal manufacturing, storage and distribution activities. ‘Drugs’ In a related discovery at the complex, the agency uncovered a warehouse on the last floor of a building containing packaging materials for suspected falsified medicines, including Augmentin 625mg and Amplicloxa. Bottle caps bearing the Gordon’s Gin brand were also reportedly found among the materials. The latest discoveries add to a series of enforcement operations by NAFDAC at the Trade Fair market. In previous raids, the agency recovered 728 cartons of Crusader soap, 718 cartons of E45 soap and quantities of Extract Gold whitening soap, products it said were banned by the Federal Government. The repeated discoveries have raised concerns about the scale of illegal product manufacturing and repackaging activities operating within the market, as well as the potential risks to unsuspecting consumers. item.title: NYSC, Army Strengthen Security Collaboration In Taraba
item.description: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) is seeking strengthened collaboration with the 10 Division, Nigeria Army, to enhance the safety and security of corps members in Taraba State. The NYSC is also commending the Nigeria Army for its sustained efforts in combating terrorism and other forms of criminality in the state. The Area Director, NYSC North East Area Office 2, Odoba Oche, stated this during a courtesy call to the General Officer Commanding 10 Division and Commander, Operation Mountain Watch, Major General Nnebeife, at headquarters 10 Division, Jalingo, Taraba State Capital. Oche, who oversees NYSC activities in Adamawa, Gombe and Taraba states, praised the Nigeria Army for unalloyed protection of orientation camps. NYSC, Army Strengthen Security Collaborations In Taraba. For Major General Nnebeife, the General Officer Commanding 10 Division, Nigeria Army, the NYSC is a critical partner in promoting National Unity and integration. According to him, both the Nigeria Army and the NYSC share a common commitment to patriotism, national cohesion and service to the nation, and fostering unity among Nigerians. The GOC assured the Area Director of the Nigeria Army’s commitment to protecting lives and property, particularly the safety of corps members during orientation exercises and movement to places of primary assignments. item.title: Nollywood sequel “Issakaba: The Return” hits cinemas after 25 years
item.description: Nollywood action thriller ‘Issakaba: The Return’ has returned to cinemas nationwide after 25 years of the release of the original movie, ‘Issakaba’. The director, Lancelot Imasuen, announced the cinema release in a post on his Instagram page on Friday, expressing excitement over the return of the popular movie franchise to the big screen. In the post, Imasuen described the production as the return of a legend and urged movie lovers to watch the film in cinemas. The sequel features veteran actor Sam Dede reprising his role as Ebube, leader of the Issakaba Boys, while introducing other actors from different generations of Nollywood. Other cast members include Chidi Mokeme, Iyabo Ojo, Regina Daniels, Chiwetalu Agu, Alex Osifo, Charles Okafor, Nosa Rex and Mark Angel. Directed by Imasuen, who also helmed the original production, ‘Issakaba: The Return’ revisits the story of the fictional vigilante group against the backdrop of contemporary Nigerian society. The original film, released in 2001, drew inspiration from the activities of the Bakassi Boys, a vigilante group that emerged in south-eastern Nigeria to combat criminal activities. The sequel, distributed by Blue Pictures, brings together returning actors and newer Nollywood performers, marking the revival of one of the industry’s recognised action film franchises. Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky told reporters Friday in comments embargoed until Saturday. He said Ukraine was discussing “specific security guarantees from NATO and the EU” and that if Western countries confirmed them “then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not? I have no right to make that decision on my own.” ‘Dangerous’ Ukraine’s Presiudent Volodymyr Zelensky said the EU and NATO are Europe’s only “real security”, warning the Kremlin’s bid to change the continent’s security architecture could lead to more wars. “This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelensky told reporters Friday in comments only releasable on Saturday. “Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That’s it. There is no other security in Europe.” Russia’ winter war Russia is “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign in its war with Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in comments released Saturday as he called for a US military package that would pressure President Vladimir Putin to end the fighting. “They are betting everything on this winter,” Zelensky told the media Friday in comments kept under embargo. item.title: I can’t insult Peter Obi; we parted ways amicably — Tanko
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The National Coordinator of the Social Democratic Party, SDP Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Yunusa Tanko, has taken a swipe at those behind viral reports circulating online alleging that he spoke ill of and used unprintable words against the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, Peter Obi, saying he cannot ever insult his former principal. The National Coordinator of Prince Adewole Adebayo and Dr Usman Bugaje’s Presidential Campaign Council described the fabricated reports as the desperate handiwork of those he described as mischief-makers and political detractors bent on sowing discord and tarnishing his hard-earned reputation. In a statement signed on Saturday by the Chief Media and Communications Advisor, Adebayo-Bugaje (Ade-Buga) Presidential Campaign Council, Comrade Mark Adebayo, Tanko explained that anyone familiar with his character and political journey knows that he is a principled, decent, and respectful individual who neither engages in blackmail nor trades in insults. He expressed complete confidence that Peter Obi would immediately dismiss the falsehoods, knowing full well the mutual respect they share. “I can never insult His Excellency, Mr Peter Obi,” Dr Tanko stated emphatically. “We parted ways peacefully and with absolute mutual understanding. Politics is about vision and service, never about bitterness or personal attacks.” Reiterating the sentiments he shared during his unveiling as the National Coordinator of the Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Tanko expressed deep appreciation and lasting gratitude to Mr Obi for the relationship they shared during his tenure as an aide and as the National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement Worldwide. “I remain forever grateful to His Excellency, Mr Peter Obi, for the wonderful opportunities he gave me to serve alongside him and lead the Obidient Movement worldwide. I thank Mr Obi, and I stand proudly by the records of my service with him,” he added. Dr Tanko, who warned purveyors of fake news that their attempts to manufacture bad blood between him and his former principal have failed before arrival, affirmed that he and the 2023 presidential candidate of the Labour Party (LP) remain the best of friends and pledged that he will continue to accord the former Anambra State Governor the utmost respect at all times. The Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council urges the general public and members of the press to disregard the malicious publications in their entirety and rely only on verified communications from the council. item.title: How lifestyle, late detection fuel diabetes crisis in Nigeria
item.description: As Nigeria joins the rest of the world to commemorate World Diabetes Day(WDD), marked annually on Nov. 14, health experts have warned that changing lifestyles and late detection are fuelling a diabetes crisis in the country. WDD is commemorated to raise awareness on prevention, early detection and care. Diabetes Mellitus, a chronic metabolic condition characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of the pancreas to produce enough insulin or impaired insulin action, has become a major public health concern, with complications including blindness, kidney failure, heart failure, stroke and limb amputation. According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) Diabetes Atlas, globally no fewer than 589 million adults live with diabetes, with 24.6 million in Africa. About 11 million adults live with the condition in Nigeria, with many unaware of their status. Experts said the disease, which could remain undetected for years without symptoms, was now killing more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined. An Endocrinologist, Prof. Michael Olamoyegun, said diabetes killed more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined. Olamoyegun is Professor of Medicine and Endocrinology at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology and also Consultant Physician and Endocrinologist at LAUTECH Teaching Hospital, Ogbomoso, Oyo State. He said diabetes is a metabolic disorder of carbohydrates, fats and protein. He added that it is characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of pancreas to produce enough insulin. According to him, diabetes also occurs if insulin action is impaired. He said there are many variants but three main types existed – Type 1, Type 2 and Gestational Diabetes. ” Type 1 diabetes, which occurs due to absolute deficiency of insulin, is seen mainly in younger age group, usually less than 30 years, although occasionally in adulthood. “It is found in about five to ten per cent of all individuals with diabetes. “This group is managed with insulin injections since the body no longer produces insulin.” The endocrinologist said Type 2 diabetes represented 90 to 95 per cent of individuals with diabetes, stressing it occurred when insulin was not able to function well in the body. He also noted that it usually occurred in older individuals who had family history in first-degree relatives. Olamoyegun, also the Secretary General of the Association of Clinical Endocrinologists of Nigeria (ACEN), added that hypertension, overweight or obesity and sedentary lifestyles were contributory risk factors. He said it is usually managed with oral medications, dietary control and occasionally with insulin. On gestational diabetes mellitus, he said it was first detected in pregnancy, saying it complicated about 7.5 to 12 per cent of all pregnancies. item.title: Airspace Now ‘Opened Up,’ No Cyberattack — US
item.description: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear. “At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.” Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. US aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country on November 13 after a major communications outage which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any “nefarious attack.” The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System. “Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?” Duffy, however, insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide. “Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said. Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.” “When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added. But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out. Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began. “President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.” Passengers wait at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington, DC on November 13, 2026. item.title: APC Women Target 10 Million Votes For Tinubu In 2027
item.description: The Women Mobilisation Committee of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has pledged to mobilise 10 million women’s votes nationwide for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. The pledge was made by the APC National Women Leader and Director of the Women Mobilisation Committee of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Mary Alile Idele, at a town hall meeting held in Gusau on Thursday. Addressing women leaders, party stakeholders and supporters from across the 14 local government areas of Zamfara State, Idele urged women to deliver massive votes for President Tinubu in recognition of the impact of his administration on their lives. She acknowledged what she described as the Tinubu administration’s achievements in transforming the lives of Nigerian women and their children, saying the government had deliberately placed women at the centre of its Renewed Hope Agenda. APC Women target 10 million votes for Tinubu in 2027 According to her, the President has demonstrated a strong commitment to women’s empowerment through policies and programmes that directly impact women in both rural and urban communities. She identified the Student Loan Scheme as one of the administration’s landmark achievements, noting that it had provided many Nigerian children, including those from disadvantaged families in Zamfara, with opportunities to pursue higher education without the burden of tuition fees. Idele also highlighted women’s empowerment initiatives, including cash grants, which she said had enabled thousands of women to establish and expand small businesses, support their families and achieve greater economic independence. She added that the distribution of starter packs to trained women had helped beneficiaries apply their acquired skills immediately, rather than returning home without the necessary tools to start their businesses. The APC National Women Leader further commended the administration’s support for women in agriculture, explaining that female farmers in Zamfara and other states had benefited from farm inputs, training and other interventions aimed at boosting food production and improving their income. Also speaking at the town hall meeting, the wife of the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Hajiya Asmau Yari, described the visit of First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu to Zamfara as historic and heartwarming. She said Mrs Tinubu was the first Nigerian First Lady to visit Zamfara State since its creation, describing the visit as a demonstration of love, respect and recognition for the women of the state. Asmau Yari urged Zamfara women to reciprocate the gesture by voting massively for President Tinubu in the 2027 general elections to enable him to consolidate on the gains already recorded by his administration. item.title: Tight security as Tinubu visits Jos for APC presidential rally
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Security has been beefed up in Jos, the Plateau State capital, ahead of the expected arrival of President Bola Tinubu on Saturday for the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally. Our correspondent, who visited several parts of the city, observed a heavy deployment of security personnel at strategic locations, including Hill Station Junction, Zaria Road, Polo Roundabout and parts of Yakubu Gowon Way, as security agencies intensified surveillance ahead of the President’s visit. Tinubu is expected to attend the APC presidential rally scheduled to hold at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos, where he is also expected to commission three major development projects executed by the Plateau State Government. The projects are the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Centre in Jos, the Plateau Special Activity Centre (P-SAC) and 50 hybrid Jet Mover buses for inter-local government transportation. Ahead of the President’s visit, Governor Caleb Mutfwang, APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, and former Deputy Governor, Dame Pauline Tallen, inspected the facilities. Speaking on the BPO Centre, Mutfwang described it as a strategic investment in human capital development, job creation and economic empowerment. According to a statement signed by his Director of Press and Public Affairs, Gyang Bere, the governor said the facility, established through a partnership between the Plateau State Government, Outsource Global and MTN Nigeria, has an operational capacity of 800 seats and is projected to generate up to 2,400 direct full-time jobs when fully deployed across three shifts. He said the centre would connect Plateau youths to the global digital economy through customer experience management, technical support and back-office services. Mutfwang added that young people would be able to work for international organisations from Jos and earn in foreign currencies. On the Plateau Special Activity Centre, the governor said the facility was established to strengthen intelligence-driven security operations, stressing that security remained fundamental to sustainable development. The centre comprises a Fusion and Analytical Centre, Geo-Intelligence/GIS Unit, Drone Unit, Training Centre and Profiling Room to enhance intelligence gathering, threat detection, analysis and coordinated security responses. He also said the 50 hybrid buses would improve public transportation, reduce travel costs and enhance connectivity across the state’s 17 local government areas. Meanwhile, during an inspection of the Zaria Road Stadium, venue of the rally, Mutfwang expressed confidence that the event would attract massive participation from APC supporters and stakeholders across the North-Central region. He urged residents to turn out in large numbers to welcome Tinubu, whom he described as a statesman committed to the development and security of Plateau State. item.title: ABSU VC bans birthday parties, awards, courtesy visits
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The newly-appointed Vice-Chancellor of Abia State University, ABSU, Uturu, Prof. Amadike Ugbogu, has banned courtesy visits by faculties and departments, birthday celebrations, award presentations and portrait gifts in his honour throughout his tenure. Read Also: (Video) UNN Party Tragedy: How I regained consciousness, found friends lying lifeless – Survivor The directive, contained in a notice issued by the University’s Media and Public Relations Unit, also prohibits the acceptance of birthday cakes and honours from individuals, organisations, churches and communities. Prof. Ugbogu appreciated the university community for the goodwill and support accorded him during his inauguration. But directed faculties and departments to discontinue courtesy visits to his office. Rather than receive delegations, the Vice-Chancellor said he would personally visit the various faculties and departments to interact with staff and acquaint himself with their activities, achievements and challenges. He also made it clear that he would not entertain birthday parties organised in his honour or accept birthday cakes. The university community, students, staff and members of the public were urged to respect and cooperate with the directives. The Vice-Chancellor who assumed office barely two weeks ago, reaffirmed his commitment to purposeful leadership, academic excellence, institutional development and the overall progress of the university. item.title: Argentina beaten by Uruguay in first game since Messi retirement
item.description: Argentina suffered a 2-1 defeat against Uruguay on Friday in their first game since Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football. A second-half own goal by Argentina defender Leonardo Balerdi followed by a fluky effort from Uruguay midfielder Maxi Araujo sealed defeat for the 2026 World Cup runners-up. Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alavarez gave Argentina hope of a comeback with a 73rd-minute strike but Uruguay held on to clinch a third victory for new manager Diego Forlan. Messi played his final game for Argentina in an emotional farewell friendly victory over Benin last month, calling time on a glittering career that spanned 207 caps and 125 goals. With the 39-year-old genius missing, Argentina struggled to break down a resilient Uruguay team for long stretches of Friday’s friendly. Nico Paz had Argentina’s best chance of the first half, but saw his shot well-saved by Uruguay goalkeeper Cristopher Fiermarin. Uruguay made the breakthrough soon after half-time when a Giorgian de Arrascaeta free-kick from the left caused chaos in the Argentina defence. Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez attempted to clear with a header but his effort instead cannoned off team-mate Balerdi and into the net. De Arrascaeta then set up Uruguay’s second in the 53rd minute, his corner appearing to hit Araujo’s shoulder before looping high into the net. Alvarez pulled a goal back midway through the half, and had another good chance in stoppage time but Uruguay closed out the win. item.title: Women and race to 2027
item.description: Going by the number of women that have emerged candidates in the last primary elections of all the political parties in Nigeria, next year’s general polls is bound to witness fewer number of women contesting elective positions. Weekend Trust reports that while more women indicated interests in contesting by obtaining forms to secure the tickets of their parties, most of them could not go beyond the preliminary stages, with many of them either withdrawing, not considered in the consensus arrangements, or defeated in the early stages. Checks by our correspondents revealed that a higher number of women had indicated interests in contesting for state assembly seats, but the number dwindled for those going for House of Representatives seats, again, dropping drastically for Senate and getting terribly low on governorship. When the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) released the names of the presidential candidates for 2027, only two out of the 18 candidates, which constitutes 11.1per cent of the total candidates, are women, despite making up 49.32 per cent of Nigeria’s population. Amidst campaigns, Borno, Niger children remain in captivity Tinubu booed at Abuja mosque after Friday prayers They are up against 15 men, including President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and other candidates across the political parties. The two women are Ada Elizabeth Okwori of the National Democratic Party (NDP) and Esther Iken Okereke of the National Rescue Movement (NRM). Also, there are four female vice presidential candidates who will be contesting. These are Hajiya Bintu Konto (LP), Ofordile Peace Egobia (APP), Nafisat Usaku (DLA) and Patience Key (YPP) INEC figures obtained by Weekend Trust, showed that 469 women are among the 4,863 candidates listed for the Senate and House of Representatives elections, while only two of the 18 presidential candidates are women. The figures indicate that fewer than one in every 10 candidates contesting the National Assembly elections is female, while women constitute just over one in every 10 presidential candidates. The Senate has the lowest female representation, with 123 women among 1,303 candidates, representing 9.4 per cent. The House of Representatives has 346 female candidates out of 3,560, representing 9.7 per cent. The figures were calculated from the party and gender fields contained in INEC’s final list of candidates. The figures reflect a pattern in Nigerian politics in which women participate extensively in elections but remain largely absent from the institutions where political decisions are made. Data from 2015 show that only one woman contested the presidency, while four women were listed as vice presidential candidates, with 14 political parties participating. item.title: World Diabetes Day: High cost pushes drugs, special diets out of reach
item.description: As the world marks the 2026 World Diabetes Day today, attention is once again drawn to the importance of early diagnosis, timely treatment and sustained care in preventing complications and saving lives. But for many Nigerians living with the condition, the challenge goes beyond early detection to affording medication, special diets and regular medical checks needed to manage the disease. Some patients who spoke to Weekend Trust said the rising cost of treatment had pushed them into financial hardship, forcing them to ration prescribed drugs, compromise their diets or go for days without medication. For Mrs Ngunengen Akpam, living with diabetes has become a daily struggle, not only against the disease but also against the rising cost of managing it. Tinubu booed at Abuja mosque after Friday prayers Women and race to 2027 The burden is compounded by her responsibility to also support her diabetic mother, Mama Lydia Acka, making the cost of medication, food and routine medical care a constant source of worry for the family. Akpam told one of our correspondents that the prices of essential diabetes medications had increased considerably over the years, making it increasingly difficult to maintain the treatment prescribed by her doctors. She recalled that Metformin, one of the drugs she takes, which sold for N700 for a pack of three cards in 2015, now costs about N2,500. Similarly, Dormin, which previously sold for N700, now costs N3,500 for a pack of 10 cards, she said. “The cost of drugs has increased tremendously. I take my medication twice daily, so it is not easy. In a month, we spend so much, especially when you have another diabetic person to cater for,” she said. Medication, however, is only part of the financial burden. Akpam explained that managing diabetes also requires adherence to a carefully regulated diet, including millet, beans and vegetables, which have also become expensive. Although the price of millet had dropped from more than N1,200 to N600 per mudu during the harvest season, she said her financial circumstances still made it difficult to consistently afford the recommended food items. The experience is similar for Mrs Elahi Onu, who has lived with diabetes for 11 years and whose treatment has become a major financial responsibility for her children. Onu said her children spend at least N25,000 monthly on medication alone, while more than N60,000 goes into providing the special diet recommended for managing her condition. She listed unripe plantain, beans, vegetables, basmati rice and grains such as millet among the food items she had been advised to eat. “These special types of food are costly and drain the pockets of my children. “Sometimes there is a delay in supplies of these items to me. I will be forced to go hungry for the period or fall back to any available food,” she said. item.title: Amidst campaigns, Borno, Niger children remain in captivity
item.description: As the campaign season hots up, families of the abducted children in Borno and Niger states are still looking up to the authorities for intervention. Weekend Trust reports that while the pupils kidnapped in Borno have spent 213 days in captivity, students abducted in Niger have also remained in the hands of their captors for more than two weeks. Today makes it 213 days of agony and sleepless nights for the families of the abducted children in Mussa and Lassa communities of Askira-Uba Local Government Area in Borno State. The78 children, including toddlers less than two years old, who were abducted following two separate operations by bandits and insurgents, are still in captivity, even as politicians intensify campaigns for political power. The nightmare began on May 15, 2026 when at least 42 pupils and students were taken from their classrooms in Mussa Primary and Secondary School. Weeks later, on June 29, another set of 36 students were abducted in Government Day Secondary School, Lassa, further escalating security concerns in the area. Women and race to 2027 How IDPs built Abuja’s largest beans market Since then, the whereabouts of the children have remained unknown, plunging the families into a state of painful trauma. The Mussa school children were abducted on the same day as the 44 pupils and teachers from a school in the Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State. But unlike the Mussa schoolchildren that have remained in captivity, the Oyo children were rescued on July 10, 2026 after 56 days in captivity after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu gave marching orders to heads of security operatives to rescue them. Weekend Trust reports that parents of the abducted pupils in Borno have on various occasions expressed frustration over what they described as “silence” from both the federal and state governments. The families are alleging that the authorities have entirely abandoned them; expressing fear that their children may have been forgotten by the same people they voted to power to protect them. The chairman of the parents of the abducted children, Mr Ishaku Suya, told our correspondent that the communities had remained in despair since the abduction of the schoolchildren. “Officially, I have not heard anything from the federal or state governments. Nobody is saying anything. And nobody has reached out to us from the side of the abductors,” he said. According to him, the mothers of the abducted children are always crying and thinking about their condition. “As men, we cannot cry, but we can’t eat food whenever we remember that our toddlers, some of them less than 2 years old, are still in the hands of their abductors. We all feel abandoned,” he said. item.title: How IDPs built Abuja’s largest beans market
item.description: Ibrahim Philemon was compelled to abandon everything he had built in his youth and flee his native Gwoza for Karu in Nasarawa State because of Boko Haram’s relentless attacks on his community. Philemon is among thousands of other farmers who fled their towns because of intensified security risks posed by Boko Haram militants. But these farmers, despite facing adversity, remained undeterred. As internally displaced persons (IDPs), they were determined to rebuild their lives after the devastation caused by Boko Haram. Today, Philemon produces over 100 bags of beans and over 50 bags of maize annually since coming to Karu in 2013 as an internally displaced person. Amidst campaigns, Borno, Niger children remain in captivity Tinubu booed at Abuja mosque after Friday prayers When Boko Haram captured Gwoza town, which had an estimated population of around 388,600 in August 2014, thousands fled immediately to many states in the country and the neighbouring towns in Cameroon. Gwoza, which is located on the fringes of Sanbisa forest, is about 135 kilometres southeast of Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State. It is marked by a hilly terrain. As farmers, the displaced persons established approximately 13 camps in Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, where they commenced agricultural activities. With an estimated population of over 20,000, according to the International Organisation for Migration in Nasarawa, the IDPs spread across farming communities in Karu and Keffi, seeking farmlands and clearing bushes and forests that were hitherto uncultivated to plant beans and maize. Some of them harvested over 200 bags of beans (cowpea) and maize. Within three years of their arrival, these displaced farmers rose from the ashes to establish one of the most vibrant grain markets on the outskirts of Abuja, the country’s capital, which today attracts buyers across the country. Setting up a beans market As they continued to record good harvests, selling their produce in good value immediately became a huge challenge that devastated many of them who were trying to find life after the colossal losses inflicted on them back home in Gwoza. That challenge gave birth to the establishment of what is today known as the foremost beans market in 2016, located in Auta Balefi, along the Abuja-Keffi expressway, about 25 kilometres from the Aso Rock Villa, before the National Agricultural Showground. They told our reporter, who spent a day with them, that farming and trading provided opportunities for them to rebuild their lives after displacement. David Yakubu, the secretary of the beans market, told Weekend Trust how the idea came about. He said the market was established after they encountered difficulties selling their agricultural produce at profitable prices in Ibadan, Oyo State.
